If $\,T\,$ is a linear transformation and $\,T\left(\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}\right)=\begin{bmatrix}-18 \\ 36\end{bmatrix}$, then find $T\left(\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}\right).$

| $\,T\left(\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}\right)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
:question/worked-solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation, it must satisfy $T(kv)=kT(v).$ Noting that $\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}=2\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\left(\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}\right) & =T\left(2\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}\right)=2T\left(\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since we're told that 

$$
T\left(\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}\right)=\begin{bmatrix}-18 \\ 36\end{bmatrix},
$$

we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}2T\left(\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}\right) & =\begin{bmatrix}-18 \\ 36\end{bmatrix} \\ T\left(\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}\right) & =\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}-18 \\ 36\end{bmatrix} \\ T\left(\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}\right) & =\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ 18\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$
